claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a related high-entropy derivative has high saturation magnetization and coercivity typically below 100 Oe.
A tailored annealing treatment can initiate controlled nanoscale secondary-phase precipitation in an initially single-phase fcc FeCoNi matrix or matched derivative.
Cr-rich or B2-type precipitates are feasible products of the proposed annealing treatment in the target fcc FeCoNi-based material.
The annealing treatment can produce precipitates while leaving the bulk structure largely fcc.
The resulting secondary phases will be nanoscale and distributed at grain boundaries or within grains.
Secondary-phase precipitation will locally modify the magnetic microstructure.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Precipitate-induced pinning will increase the energy barrier for magnetic-domain-wall motion.
Increasing the barrier to domain-wall motion will raise coercivity relative to the homogeneous fcc state.
The annealed, precipitate-containing material will have coercivity significantly above 100 Oe.
Secondary-phase formation may cause a modest reduction in saturation magnetization.
An optimized narrow annealing window can enhance coercivity without causing complete transformation to a non-fcc structure.
Precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction can be optimized to enhance coercivity without deteriorating soft-magnetic properties.

contradictions.description: The intervention states that precipitation occurs without altering the overall fcc matrix composition, but formation of compositionally distinct Cr-rich or B2 precipitates normally requires local solute partitioning and therefore changes the residual matrix composition, even if total bulk composition is conserved.

The prediction seeks coercivity significantly above 100 Oe, while the boundary says soft-magnetic properties should not deteriorate. Because low coercivity is a defining soft-magnetic property, these statements conflict unless preservation is explicitly limited to other properties such as saturation magnetization.
